# Gezhi Matrix (格致矩阵)
> *gewu zhizhi* (格物致知, "investigate things to extend knowledge"). Arrange any two dimensions into a
grid, and at every intersection "investigate each thing to exhaust its principle" (即物穷理), generating
one deduction per cell.
Lay a row axis and a column axis out as a 2-D grid — the two axes can be anything: mental models, sc
enario constraints, characters, timelines, hexagrams… Click any intersection and the current model g
enerates a deduction report, saved into the workspace at `data/matrix.json`.
The technical package name is still `@local/creative-matrix`, the tool id is still `creative_matrix`
, and the route is still `/creative-matrix/api`; only the display name changed — no migration or rei
e is still `/creative-matrix/api`; only the display name changed — no migration or reinstall needed.
## The Name
**Gezhi** (格致) is short for *gewu zhizhi* (格物致知, "investigate things to extend knowledge"). **Ge** (
格) is a pun: it means both the individual cells of a matrix and the act of investigating/pursuing a
thing to the bottom in *gewu*; **zhi** (致) means arriving at, and **zhi** (知) means knowledge. Toget
her: investigate things cell by cell, and thereby arrive at knowledge.
This panel turns exactly that act into a table: the two axes can be anything — the row axis is **thi
ngs** (mental models, concepts, everyday objects), the column axis is **contexts** (scenarios, const
raints, situations); switch to another template and you get another pair of dimensions. Each interse
ction is one act of *jiwu qiongli* ("investigating each thing to exhaust its principle") — not gluin
g two words together, but letting one dimension deduce the consequences it must necessarily produce
her, but letting one dimension deduce the consequences it must necessarily produce inside the other.
Its original name was "Creative Matrix" (创意矩阵). The rename is not rebranding: "creative" describes t
he output, "gezhi" describes the method; and what is genuinely scarce about this plugin is the latte
output, "gezhi" describes the method; and what is genuinely scarce about this plugin is the latter.
One more detail worth recording. Zhu Xi read *gewu* as exhaustively investigating the principle of e
very thing in the world, cell by cell, outward; Wang Yangming actually went to investigate the bambo
o in front of his pavilion — seven days of it, until he fell ill — and finally said "天下之物本无可格者，其格物之功
只在身心上做" ("there are fundamentally no things under heaven to investigate; the work of investigation i
s done only on mind and body"). This matrix stands on Zhu Xi's side — it believes that arranging the
world into cells and deducing them one by one can force out something real; but it also remembers W
ang Yangming's challenge, which is why every cell must state "under what conditions this fails," and
deep mode runs an extra independent red-team pass. The name carries its own warning: what comes out
of the cells may be a beautiful deduction, not necessarily true knowledge.
## Methodology
### The four steps
1. **Set the axes** (立格): define the row axis first. Each row is a "thing" — a mental model, a mecha

nism, an everyday object. Rows must be concrete and deducible; don't write adjectives.
[该节后续省略]
### Why causal deduction, not word-pairing
If "apple × breakfast table" only ever produces "an apple sits on the breakfast table," that is pair
ing, not gezhi. Gezhi demands: treat the row axis as a causal law (apples oxidize, roll, become ritu
al), and let it necessarily produce consequences inside the column axis (the time pressure of breakf
ast, family relations, morning attention). The product should be a piece of reasoning that can be re
futed — not a pretty association.
### What it does not do
- No divination promises. The I Ching template uses the 64 hexagrams purely as thinking tools and pr

edicts no fortune.
- No "interdisciplinarity" as decoration. Every cell must answer: what judgment d

id this dimension actually change here?
- No pursuit of sudden "illumination" in a single cell. Cohe
rence is seen only much later, looking back — one cell cannot give it to you.
## Features
- **Row axis / column axis**: by default everyday concepts like apple, water, shadow × breakfast tab
le, rainy day, playground. The header shows each axis item's title and blurb; click a title to renam
e it, click the blurb to edit it — blurbs also feed into the prompt. Adding and deleting axes also h

appens in the header.
- **Three views**: below the page header are three tabs — Templates / Matrix /
Prompt. The default tab is Templates; after you pick one and load it, the panel jumps to the Matrix
automatically. In the Matrix tab you can edit the theme, axis names, axis blurbs, and add/remove ax
es; templates and prompts no longer open as modals — switching tabs gives you a full-page workspace.

Only the current tab is mounted, and unsaved drafts are discarded when you switch away.
- **Header
controls**, left to right: a **Model** dropdown (lists every provider / model DSH can reach, includi
ng local NInfer and Strata; each matrix remembers its own model — choosing "Follow default model" re
turns to DSH's default selection), a **Concurrency** dropdown (0 = all at once, or 1/2/3/4/6/8/12),
a **Save template** button, **Refresh**, and a ⋯ menu (export Markdown; a "Batch generate…" dialog,

which likewise offers a checkbox for generating only empty cells, checked by default).
- **Theme in
the top-left corner**: the top-left cell of the grid shows this matrix's theme; click it to edit in
place (Enter / blur saves, Esc cancels). Below the theme sit an "Include generated cells" checkbox a
nd a whole-matrix "Generate all" button: solid brand color, by default filling only empty cells; onc
e checked, the button becomes "Regenerate everything", redoing every cell and overwriting existing c

ontent. While a batch runs, the same button shows "Generating x/y · Stop".
- **Each axis carries its
own generate button**: every row/column header has a "▷ Generate" button and an "All" checkbox; by
default only empty cells on that axis are generated, while checking "All" regenerates the whole axis
. The neighboring "×" deletes the axis after two clicks to confirm (at least 1 row and 1 column must

"×" deletes the axis after two clicks to confirm (at least 1 row and 1 column must remain).
